v1.21.0 moves the graph engine. Every graph now runs on LadybugDB 0.22.1, the database files
carry upstream's `.lbdb` name, and the migration that gets an existing deployment there is part of
the release: export on the old engine, deploy, import on the new one, with the files renamed on
the way through. Around the engine move, the 1.20 series finished what it started: a group
member can leave as well as join, a month cannot close over an account the statements cannot see,
every operator run leaves a record, and a graph deleted mid-period is credited for the time it did
not run.

Covers everything since v1.20.0; the 1.20.x patches carried generated changelogs.

## The engine move

**LadybugDB 0.22.1.** The engine moves from 0.18.1 to 0.22.1, which fixes the query shapes the
platform had been working around: a second `OPTIONAL MATCH` after a null row returns the right
rows, a nested relationship extend no longer leaves stale filter state behind, and a multi-key
sort no longer drops rows past a few thousand scanned. The client-side sort tiebreaker that
guarded the last of those is gone; the engine's own `ORDER BY` is tested against a real database
in the suite instead. The vector extension is pinned to the matching build, and the one sort shape
the engine still gets wrong, a nullable key under a `LIMIT`, is recorded as an expected failure so
its fix will be noticed.

**Database files are `.lbdb`.** New databases, backups (`.lbdb.zip`), the published shared
repositories (`sec.lbdb`) and the public dump all use upstream's suffix. The old `.lbug` suffix is
still read wherever an archive or a legacy file can appear, so a backup taken before this release
restores, and a replica on the previous image downloads the file its own engine opens.

**The migration is a job, and it carries everything.** `ladybug_migration_export_job` checkpoints
every database on a writer, exports it on the old engine and keeps a raw copy in S3;
`ladybug_migration_import_job` renames the old file aside, imports on the new engine, verifies node
and relationship counts against the manifest, and restores the old file under its original name if
anything fails. Both connections load the vector extension, so HNSW indexes travel with the graph.
A writer on the new engine refuses a legacy file rather than opening it, so the import follows the
deploy directly. Building an HNSW index reopens the graph's pooled connections afterwards, so a
connection opened before the index existed never answers from the catalog it opened with.

**The read fleet moves on its own schedule.** A shared replica reads the database suffix from the
image it is pinned to, so the fleet can hold the previous engine while the shared master rebuilds
on the new one, then cross in one roll. A replica that cannot boot now says so to CloudFormation at
once instead of letting the stack wait out its timeout.

## The group finishes its lifecycle

**A member leaves.** `update-entity(left_on=…)` lets a member out of the group at a month end,
with guards that name what is unsettled: books not closed through that month, a bank feed still on
its chart, an intercompany balance the group disagrees with. `record-deconsolidation` books the
exit in the consolidation entity, and the group statements for the first month without the member
drop its facts, hold its closing balances at zero and show the consideration as cash divested.
`is_former` on the entity says when the month of leaving is over.

**Sales within the method, and the right gain.** `record-ownership-change` sells shares as well
as buying them, and a second change reads the premium the first one left. A member sold out of
the group, and the parent's gain on a sale that keeps control, book to the stock-in-subsidiary
gain concept rather than the property, plant and equipment one. The exemplar company gained an
acquired café, with the rows its lifecycle needed, and the demo samples were regenerated on it.

**Concept labels are pinned.** Every concept the ledger posts to carries the label the statements
print, so a taxonomy year cannot change what a posted row is called.

## The close and the statements

**An unmapped account with postings holds the close.** An account with balances and no mapping to
a reporting concept appears in no statement and no consolidating entry; until now the month closed
over it. The close now refuses until the account is mapped, naming it, and the gate reads the
parent's unlinked chart as well as its own.

**A stale graph says so, and an incomplete build never goes live.** Every freshness lookup fails
soft, a read of a graph behind its ledger carries the staleness, and a materialization that did
not finish is never swapped in.

## Operators

**Every run is recorded.** An operator run writes a durable row with its transcript: one entry per
model call, the output blocks, stop reason, usage and credits, the system prompt's hash and the
tools offered. Runs group into threads, and a request with no history is seeded from its thread's
last exchanges. `GET /v1/graphs/{g}/audit/threads`, `/audit/runs` and `/audit/runs/{operation_id}`
read them back: a graph admin reads every user's, any other member their own. The record holds the
tenant's own graph data on the same encrypted database and under the same retention as documents.

## Billing

**A graph deleted mid-period is credited.** An immediate `delete-graph` on a card-billed
subscription cancels with proration, so the unused time lands as a credit on the next invoice;
an invoice-billed graph has the unused part of its line credited, and an admin backfill credits
graphs deleted before this release.

## SEC

**Canonical concepts come from a curated table.** `Element.canonical_concept` on the `sec` graph
is stamped at staging from a curated qname table instead of an embedding match, which had put
standard equity and real-estate elements into the wrong concepts at full confidence. The first
nightly run after the deploy backfills the stamp. The MCP tools stop recommending canonical
concepts as a way to compute numbers; the filer's own elements are the path.

## Security

Input validation and authorization were hardened on the query, schema, cross-app sign-on and MCP
surfaces following an independent platform review, and a cross-app handoff now completes only in
the browser that started it.

## Fixes

- A connection's `entity_id` is the entity whose books it keeps.
- A graph-scoped API key no longer audits as an invalid key.
- The OAuth consent read says whether a fixed graph can be granted.
- The demos run end to end again and their samples carry lineage.
- Operator registration logs at debug.

## Infrastructure

- The engine image pins the LadybugDB extension repository by digest.
- The replica stack's bootstrap signals a failed boot to CloudFormation; the replica stack is
  updated by this deploy.
- The ADOT collector's debug exporter is dropped (the API stack is updated by this deploy).
- Migrations run on the orchestrator's boot: on the platform database, the operator run record;
  on the extensions database, a ticker unique among an owner's entities, the equity movements for
  a deconsolidated and an acquired interest, and the subsidiary-sale gain row, each with the
  tenant resync that carries it.
- Dependency bumps: authlib, dnspython, msgpack, filelock, pypdf, graphql-core.

Deploying this release to an existing environment is a migration, not a restart: pin the shared
replicas to the previous image, run the export job on the old engine, deploy, run the import job,
rebuild the shared repository on the new engine, then move the replica pin. The runbook for the
sequence lives with the operators of each deployment.
